name: HOTAS BF6 Simple
tagline: A fast, low-latency Windows HOTAS mapper built around Battlefield 6 and vJoy.
summary: HOTAS BF6 Simple maps a physical DirectInput controller, initially the Thrustmaster T.Flight HOTAS One, into the virtual controls Battlefield 6 can reliably bind through vJoy. It combines deterministic real-time input processing with profiles, advanced response curves, button and POV routing, automation, diagnostics, multiple UI themes, and a native installer/updater.
purpose: The project exists to make HOTAS input practical in Battlefield 6 without placing UI work, network work, allocation-heavy logic, or persistence on the mapper hot path.

principles.name: Mapper-first performance
principles.description: Input processing and vJoy output are isolated from the QML UI. Configuration is compiled outside the report loop and swapped in between reports.

principles.name: Deterministic behavior
principles.description: Profiles, automation, button controls, POV routing, and axis transforms use explicit precedence and bounded runtime state rather than timing-sensitive UI logic.

principles.name: Safe output states
principles.description: Mapping Off, controller loss, disabled routes, and unsupported virtual outputs resolve to deliberate parked or centered states instead of leaving stale commands active.

principles.name: Configuration without hot-path cost
principles.description: Rich editing, live graphs, readable automation summaries, and themes operate in presentation/configuration layers and do not add per-report UI work.

principles.name: Capability-aware hardware integration
principles.description: vJoy axes, buttons, and POV capacity are discovered at runtime. The app exposes only available targets and warns when the virtual device is undersized.

principles.name: Conservative dependency handling
principles.description: vJoy and HidHide are detected and may be offered when missing, but installed components are not silently reconfigured, downgraded, or replaced.

signalPath: Axis inversion and response curve lookup
Profile-owned output limits and axis domain
Safe routing to available vJoy axes, buttons, and POVs
Battlefield 6 binding to the virtual vJoy device
usage: Install the latest HOTAS BF6 setup package from GitHub Releases.
Configure vJoy Device 1 with the axes, button count, and POV capacity you intend to use.
Optionally configure HidHide so Battlefield sees the vJoy device while HOTAS BF6 can still read the physical controller.
Open HOTAS BF6, verify the physical controller and vJoy readiness indicators, then select or create a profile.
Configure axis routes, domains, output limits, curves, button routes, POV behavior, and game-facing labels.
Use Mapping On/Off controls and Diagnostics to confirm neutral behavior before binding controls in Battlefield 6.
Add Automation only after the base mapping is behaving correctly; new rules begin as disabled drafts and must validate before they can run.

testedStack.notes: DirectInput axes, buttons, and POV input are the project's initial supported hardware path.
Runtime capability discovery supports X, Y, Z, Rx, Ry, Rz, Slider 0, Slider 1, buttons, and continuous/discrete POVs when exposed.
The mapper exists to present bindable vJoy inputs and safe centered/one-sided axis behavior to BF6.
Used to hide the physical controller from games while keeping it visible to the mapper when configured correctly.
Windows 10/11 are supported by the current application requirements.
Core, Gui, Network, Qml, Quick, QuickControls2, and Test are used by the project.
